key_insight: The paper combines POD-based model reduction, semi-smooth Newton solvers, and neural-network corrections to efficiently solve nonlinear parametric variational inequalities while preserving primal-dual complementarity structure.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster surrogate simulation for computational mechanics problems such as obstacle and frictional contact models, where high-fidelity nonlinear solves are too expensive for repeated queries or design loops.
method: Builds reduced primal-dual models using POD snapshots from both primal and dual variables.
Augments the linear reduced space with two feedforward networks that learn nonlinear corrections in truncated coordinates.
Uses sparse cubature hyper-reduction via greedy nonnegative least squares to cut online residual costs.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical tests on a 2D obstacle problem and a 3D frictional contact problem, comparing full-order, linear reduced, neural-augmented reduced, and hyper-reduced variants.
watch_item: The learned nonlinear manifold and hyper-reduction must be carefully coupled, since approximation quality and Newton convergence can degrade if the reduced basis or cubature set is insufficient.
paper_title: A Hyper-Reduced Neural Network-Augmented Semi-smooth Newton Method for Nonlinear Parametric Variational Inequalities
